item.title: Kennedy Center board votes to restore Trump's name on building
item.description: The Kennedy Center's board of trustees voted to add President Trump's name to the facade of the performing arts center, more than two months after a judge ordered its removal, according to a Democrat who sits on the center's board.

item.title: Running Dry: The fight for the West's dwindling water supply | 60 Minutes Archive
item.description: The nation's largest reservoir, Lake Mead, has fallen to a record low. In 2021, Bill Whitaker visited the Colorado River and reported on how millions of people depend on the water to drink, power their homes, and irrigate their farms.

item.title: State Police investigators testify about search history in Lindsay Clancy trial
item.description: Lindsay Clancy's trial for the murders of her three children in Massachusetts resumed Thursday with testimony from State Police investigators.

item.title: Luigi Mangione in discussions about possible guilty plea, sources say
item.description: Luigi Mangione, accused in the 2024 killing of UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson, is in discussions about a possible plea deal on federal charges, sources familiar with the matter told CBS News.

item.title: Indiana under state of emergency after storms bring devastating floods
item.description: Indiana Gov. Mike Braun has declared a state of emergency after parts of his state saw record rainfall totals that led to floods on Wednesday. CBS News' Meg Oliver and Jessica Burch have more.

item.title: "CBS Sunday Morning" launches new series of live events at the 92nd Street Y in NYC, debuting with Sylvester Stallone
item.description: America's #1 Sunday morning news program announces a new collaboration beginning Sept. 28 to bring conversations with the biggest newsmakers in the arts, politics and culture to the stage, and streamed online.

item.title: Inside the increasing values of sports franchises amid the Lakers $12.5 billion sale
item.description: News broke on Wednesday that the Los Angeles Lakers will be sold to Bob Iger and Josh Kushner for $12.5 billion. Mike Vorkunov, national NBA and basketball business reporter for the Athletic, joins CBS News to discuss.

item.title: Record-breaking heat takes mounting toll on the U.S. economy
item.description: Heat waves are dealing a financial blow to businesses and creating hazardous conditions for workers, according to climate experts.

item.title: Ebola outbreak in Congo could be deadliest ever, global health chief warns
item.description: Dr. Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, the head of the World Health Organization, is warning that the Ebola outbreak in Congo could be the deadliest ever. CBS News' Ramy Inoncencio reports.

item.title: Baby in surrogate dispute now in custody of parents, lawyer says
item.description: The baby at the center of a surrogacy dispute was born in Texas Wednesday and has hypoplastic left heart syndrome, a rare heart defect.

item.title: Tehran says Strait of Hormuz "under Iran's control" after Trump threat
item.description: Tehran has asserted that the Strait of Hormuz is "under Iran's control and management" after President Trump said the U.S. might "keep it."

item.title: They've survived 2 major earthquakes in Colombia: "A sense of powerlessness"
item.description: Colombia earthquake survivors are facing major loss and a yearslong road to recovery filled with grief and uncertainty. Here's what responders say will happen next.

item.title: Trump's secret plane switch took place within a day of credible missile threat
item.description: President Trump secretly moved from Air Force One to another plane within a day of U.S. and Turkish intelligence picking up on an Iranian plot to fire a missile at the jet, CBS News has learned.

item.title: What's a good 1-year CD account interest rate considered to be now?
item.description: With the interest rate climate uneven, it helps to know what a good 1-year CD account interest rate is considered to be.

item.title: Democratic senators demand answers about conditions aboard USS Abraham Lincoln
item.description: Senate Democrats are demanding answers about conditions aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln during the aircraft carrier's record-setting deployment.

item.title: Tropical storm forms near Hawaii, hurricane watch issued for the Big Island
item.description: Tropical Storm Lala could bring rain, high winds, and dangerous surf and rip currents to the Hawaiian Islands this weekend.

item.title: Trump administration's antisemitism lawsuit against Harvard dismissed
item.description: The lawsuit was one of many steps against Harvard that the Trump administration has taken since President Trump's return to office, in addition to attempting to cancel billions of dollars in federal funds.

item.title: Can taking weight-loss drugs help you get hired? Yes, if you're a woman.
item.description: Going on GLP-1 drugs significantly boosted unemployed women's chances of finding a job, according to a Harvard economist.

item.title: Surrogate gives birth to baby at center of multistate legal battle
item.description: Surrogate McKenna West declined to get an abortion requested by the intended parents after the baby she was carrying was diagnosed with a severe but treatable heart defect.

item.title: Floodwaters submerge Midwest neighborhoods bracing for more severe storms
item.description: Muddy floodwaters seeped into the homes of Indiana and Ohio residents this week, as severe storms struck the Midwest. Now, some areas are bracing for even more rain.

item.title: Sources say sailor from USS Lincoln went overboard last month, families sound alarm about conditions
item.description: Two sources tell CBS News a sailor on the USS Lincoln went overboard last month. They were pulled from the water safely, but the moment comes as some family members say they're concerned about conditions aboard the ship. CBS News' Reed Cowan reports.

item.title: Acton teen held without bail in murders of mother, brother linked to ChatGPT
item.description: An Acton, Massachusetts teenager charged with killing his mother and brother in a case linked to ChatGPT is being held without bail.

item.title: Explaining the charges against Nick Reiner, who is accused of killing parents Rob and Michele
item.description: Nick Reiner has been indicted on murder charges in the killings of his parents, Rob and Michele Reiner. CBS News' Katrina Kaufman explains the charges.

item.title: 3 reasons to switch your money market account now
item.description: In today's unique economic climate, a switch from your money market account may make a lot of sense. Here's why.

item.title: Becky G reflects on advocacy in new music, rise to fame
item.description: Becky G spoke exclusively with "CBS Mornings" co-host Gayle King about her rise to fame, being the breadwinner of the family at a young age and her new music.

item.title: Cities propose new tactics to crack down on so-called "teen takeovers"
item.description: Large gatherings of young people, often spurred by online invites, can lead to violence and injuries, even death.

item.title: 60 cats rescued from abandoned boat anchored off Washington state
item.description: Police in Tacoma, Washington, say they have rescued 60 cats and kittens from an abandoned sailboat that was found anchored off a city beach last week.

item.title: My Uncle Joe's Murder
item.description: A young woman mourns her uncle's murder … and questions whether the convicted killer was the only one involved. "48 Hours" contributor Nikki Battiste reports.

item.title: Facing a Monster
item.description: A teenager survives a vicious attack by an ex-boyfriend. Years later, she faces him in court after he murders a young mother. "48 Hours" correspondent Anne-Marie Green reports.

item.title: Why Smart People Fall for Scams | Money Moves with Jill Schlesinger
item.description: Jill and Mark discuss a $50 million Ponzi scheme that ensnared dozens of investors with promises of big, risk-free returns. Then, they break down the emotional manipulation tactics scammers use to gain your trust and how to protect yourself as AI makes fraud more sophisticated and harder to spot than ever. Plus, a burned-out caller is desperate for a career reset and wonders how long she can afford to coast on her savings before figuring out her next move.
